utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, bring in the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can everyone hear me? On the side of the Prosecution, can you hear me? On the side of the Defence, Mr. Blaskic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour; I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Sit down please. My colleagues can hear me. Thank you. Then we are ready to resume our work, where we interrupted our work roughly two weeks ago. We are now in the stage of the Prosecution which is to tell us where we now stand. I think we have to finish the cross-examination of a witness; is that so? Very well. Perhaps we can bring in the witness. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, Mr. Djidic is in the waiting room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, good morning. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I should like to remind you you are still under oath and I think we can now continue and I hope complete the cross-examination. Mr. Nobilo or Mr. Hayman? It is Mr. Nobilo. MR. SEFKIJA DJIDIC (continued)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours, my learned colleagues. Good morning Mr. Djidic. It was two weeks ago where we stopped when we were talking about some front lines around Vitez where we located the positions of the BH-Army. This was about 16th April 1993 that we were talking about. Can you tell us whether those front lines were moved later on, for instance in May 1993? Were there any changes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first days of war consisted of constant attacks and then in May there were offences and counter-offences, and then I think it was in August that the HVO captured Grbavica. I do not exactly recall the date when that happened. The army captured Zabrdje and those were the lines that were maintained until the end of the war with only minor changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You spoke to us last time about the 325th Brigade and their positions. Could you tell us anything about the 306th brigade from Han Bila and its participation in the battles in the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly who took part in the fighting. I said that I was under encirclement and that I received only information that concerned me regarding Stari Vitez. It is possible that the 306th also participated, but I do not know the exact locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But were you connected by phone or radio links with the Third Corps while you were surrounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in touch with the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And with no one else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one else directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what the Seventh Muslim Brigade was doing on the front around Poculice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The 17th Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that it was in the territory of Vitez during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you were not in touch with anyone from the Third Corps but on 16th April 1993, did you have a telephone conversation with Enver Hadzihasanovic, the commander of the Third Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That was the day of the attack in the morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go back to the part of your statement relating to the capture of the military policemen in Krusica. You spoke to Pasko Lubicic and Blaskic; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you personally guaranteed with your own life that there would be investigations and only then did the people from Krusica release the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to know how come you had to guarantee with your life, why could you not simply order the release of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time I could not issue such an order because two members of the army were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I do not understand; they were dead, yes, but you were the commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does that mean? Would they refuse to follow your orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They found it very difficult to carry out my orders and until I guaranteed that there would be an investigation and probably this must have been agreed between Mr. Merdan and Mr. Blaskic, and Merdan guaranteed that there would be an investigation the very next morning, and when I explained to these men that there would be an investigation, then they agreed to release the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, we realised that, but what I am interested in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, again before we get too far on this, I do object to the form of the questions as to what he realises and what he does not understand. I just ask Mr. Nobilo to ask questions and I object to the form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained. Mr. Nobilo, you have your own views regarding the way in which the witness is answering questions, but you can use his answers the way you wish, but you cannot make any personal comments, therefore just questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will continue if I may, but let me just explain: I was not commenting; the witness did not answer my question. He answered with a statement that he had already given, but I will follow your instructions. I would like to know whether the organisation of the BH-Army in your region at the time was such that you could issue an order which would be followed without discussion or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means that they should have followed my orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But they did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is why I was angry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go on. You said that you were informed about civilians captured and detained in the veterinary station; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember where those civilians were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Rijeka and Sofa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there any fighting in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was no fighting; people were simply arrested in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where is Rijeka in relation to Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is about one kilometre away from Stari Vitez roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know any names of people who were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Dr Zeco Fuad, Pasaga Mujanovic, his two sons and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After they were arrested, did they attack you from that direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, you cannot say; the attack comes from the Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was anybody wounded or killed in the veterinary station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that some civilians from Gacice were also incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were in incarcerated in one of the schools in Kolonija. I am not quite sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, were there any attacks from the direction of Gacice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that direction, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You also said from the locality of Novaci, some families were in prison in Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After the HVO captured Novaci, were there any attacks from that direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you respond to those attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were defending ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your estimate, would those civilians have been safer in Novaci or in the school in Dubravica? Where were they safer in view of the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those civilians were detained, some of them, in the school in Dubravica and some of them in several cellars in Novaci. I do not know where their safety would have been better, but they were arrested when Novaci had already been captured, when the army moved to Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that in three or four months all the civilians, that is Muslims, were expelled from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell me: how do you know that they were expelled rather than having gone themselves to places where there was no fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received reports to that effect from international organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was stated at meetings that a certain group had been expelled, that another group had been transferred and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you have no direct knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see it. I only know when the exchange took place, the exchange of those captured in the cinema and in the chess club.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You also said that you, Mario Cerkez, a catholic priest, and the Muslim Hadzi had to visit the checkpoints and roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How come you and Cerkez did not simply issue orders rather than going from one checkpoint to another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an agreement that we had that we should go there together and that we should jointly persuade people to remove the roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said "to persuade people", but that does not sound very military-like to me. Could you not issue a joint order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with you that it was not a military kind of operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why did the priest and the Hadzi have to go? They were not part of the military structure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were influential in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And if you had not gone there together with the priest and the Hadzi, would the orders have been executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If those orders would have been carried out, why then did they have to go with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were attempts of us to establish some kind of community amongst us, to do something together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: During the cross-examination, you said in answer to my assertion that Blaskic had his own responsibility within the operative zone of Central Bosnia which he was the commander of, that this was imagined so. What did you imply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If necessary, I can find the citation from the transcript. When I asked you and mentioned that Blaskic was the commander of the operative zone of Central Bosnia, you answered that his operative zone of Central Bosnia was something imaginary, that it was not real.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that answer at all; it was not imaginary, it was real.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me cite the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I think we will find a way out with difficulty if you make comments on your own cross-examination. I am not opposed to you asking that question again, but I would like to draw your attention to the rather tricky character. You are asking a question to the witness 58 days later regarding his own answer, not an answer to a question put to the Prosecution, but in answer to a question you yourself made. I think you must deduce from the answer made by the witness at the time if he said "imaginary". I do not think we can dwell too long now on commentaries. You may not have been satisfied with the answer he made, but that was the answer he gave you, so please rephrase it otherwise. You cannot comment on your own cross-examination; it is not done. Do you understand what I am trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I did not wish to comment on my own cross-examination; I wished to elaborate on the answer of the witness. He said that it was imaginary, and I am trying to refresh his memory. If he had recalled, I would have elaborated on the answer, but if he cannot remember, I can go on and I will not come back to that question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that the witness answers questions. Whether those answers satisfy you or not, those are the rules of the game, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, I will go on. I would like to know where your ammunition depot was in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was close to Lasva in Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In which building was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was underground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It was not a building; it was a dug-out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a dug-out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell me: what was the quantity of ammunition you had at your disposal at the time of the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that a certain amount of ammunition was held in private homes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the soldiers that had certain combat sets. Of course, the ammunition should be with the man operating it, with the soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The ammunition that was held in houses or held by the military, did you collect it in the warehouse or did you just have a record of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a record of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When people went into battle, could they take that ammunition from their own homes or did they have to go to a central warehouse each time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That depended on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that they could go to the central warehouse but they could also take the ammunition from their own homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They only had combat sets that went with the weapon they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the attack occurred on 16th April 1993, did you have any artillery support from the BH-Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I still did not have any such support.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have mortar support?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did you get artillery support?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was on the second or third day that I got a little support.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You had a mortar, as you said. Did you target Blaskic's headquarters on 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know what targets the RPG and the mortar were directed against on 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the RPG was not used on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you subsequently mobilised the people who were surrounded in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was the situation as regards uniforms? Did everyone have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that women were mobilised too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of assignments did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women worked as nurses in infirmaries and they were cooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They did not have any direct military assignments in the narrower sense?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When your headquarters was hit, you moved, of course. Did you mark that building in any way so that one could know that it was the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where the army was housed, were those buildings marked in any special ways?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you are aware that there was an offer to the civilians to leave Stari Vitez temporarily. I want to know how you learned about this offer from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received an ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But technically how was it done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through the media, on the loudspeaker system and through UN members, members of the United Nations force.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While you were surrounded, was there any kind of civilian political body representing the civilians in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Civil Defence system existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am thinking of a political body of authority.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did civilians have any kind of representative who would represent the civilians as opposed to the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the President of the SDA party, the President of the local community. Then there was Merhamet, which provided relief for the civilian population and representatives of the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you mention some names who held those positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Munir Kajnovic was the President of the SDA, Zara Halilovic was the President of Merhamet, a lady, Adem Jelaskovic and Edo Arnautovic were representatives of the Civil Defence. This was kind of a Civil Defence staff, I remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This body of civilian defence, this headquarters, this staff: did you propose to them they get out; was it discussed at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On 16th April 1993, can you tell us what is the farthest point that the HVO soldiers reached in their attack and during the day? Did they go back at all; can you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question. The HVO soldiers on the first day came from the church to the home of Edo Arnautovic. Across the street from his house is the house of Zvonko Mlakic. From the Mlakics, the HVO soldiers had come into Remiza settlement, the Remiza settlement near the stadium, but during the day they returned from the direction of Kolonija. HVO soldiers, they torched five or six houses near the garages, and after that, they returned. The HVO soldiers, coming from the Pavlovic houses, came to the power supply building and that is where they stayed. Those were approximately the lines that remained until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we therefore conclude that the HVO was returned from three directions and the front was stabilised at those points that they reached?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All Vitez was attacked from all sides. One can say, generally speaking, that they were stopped from those directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: During your statement, you said that ten civilians were shot by snipers. Did you personally see a situation when a civilian was killed by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Directly, no, I did not see one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that 15 civilians were killed "by Beba, as we called them". Did you personally see any civilians lose their lives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the Grizovic house was attacked. I personally took these women out of that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you come to that place after it was hit, or were you there before the explosion occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came after it was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where is the Grizovic house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Grizovic house is near the stadium and the garages, about 50 metres away from the garages, towards Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your units, where were they, if you look at the Grizovic house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How near?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30 or 40 metres; the closest soldier was 30 or 40 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is there any kind of building between that house and the closest soldiers that were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a settlement that is densely populated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question is: between the soldiers that were standing there, the soldier who was standing the closest to the Grizovic house, was there another house between the two or was it just empty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was another house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many houses and what house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not too sure, but I am sure there were three or four houses in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you said they were hit by sniper, did you see any livestock, cattle, being hit by sniper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw horses, cows, sheep that were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many horses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two horses were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Cows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sheep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten-odd sheep.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In about ten or fifteen attempts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, is that very important for the Defence of General Blaskic, to ascertain the number of cows that were hit? If you say no, then please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is important, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, continue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is important, but we could give more detailed explanations only to your Honours, not in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You said it is important to ascertain the number of cows, sheep and horses that were killed, so continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, did you know Professor Jozic? He taught at the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you referring to Boro Jozic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Emira from Vitez is his wife.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you know him well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the Chairman of the Commission for Exchanges in the time of encirclement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know that he was killed by sniper fire in front of his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know that in front of that house, that is the grey building near the bus station in Partisanska Street, a girl called Amela, 20 years old, was killed by sniper fire from old Vitez? Pavlovic, 18 years old? Did you know that 103 persons, most of them civilians, were killed in Vitez by sniper from old Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you ever issue such orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have snipers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was there any discussions related to snipers when you talked to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was this about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mainly it was we who insisted, we explained about snipers of the HVO that were hitting and had we been asked whether we had a sniper, we would have showed it. It was an old sniper, and we mostly used it for fighting against snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR inform you that General Blaskic on 20th April 1993 ordered all HVO snipers to be collected, closed up in a warehouse and to sign these orders and he also authorised UNPROFOR to kill whoever fired a sniper and who had a sniper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard something about this warning that was issued to the HVO, but I do not know about this concretely, specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you did not hear about Blaskic's orders to kill any people who were shooting a sniper by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who were firing snipers in your army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a refugee; I cannot remember who he was. I cannot remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Omanovic Hida, was that the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Katarovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you had a mortar. Could soldiers use these mortars whichever way they wanted or did you have to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had to be under my orders because we had very few grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you ever issue orders to operate with a mortar against civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did subordinates ever do that without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not too sure, but I do not think they did, because really we had very few grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, your Honours, I kindly request that we look at a videocassette now. These are atrocities that are videotaped, so if there are any people in the audience who cannot take that, I would request them to leave. We are not happy to show this, but this is a mortar that killed several people in Vitez. I kindly request the technicians to show the videocassettes. As far as the interpreters are concerned, we gave a text and you will hear the sound from the videotape, so kindly interpret it directly. Perhaps the lights could be turned off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before giving you the floor and before switching off the lights, first the Chamber will decide whether we are going to allow the showing of this tape. (Pause). At the request of my colleague Mr. Shahabudden, I am going to ask you: are you going to ask for this tape to be admitted into evidence, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will give you the floor in a moment, Mr. Prosecutor. The Trial Chamber does not wish to exclude the public; it was correct of you to issue the warning. It is up to the public gallery to decide whether they will watch or not. Mr. Prosecutor, do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, I have two issues, your Honour. The first is the source of the film. The second is a presentation from counsel as to the relevance of this film, given the defendant and these charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your objections are sustained. Will you please tell us, Mr. Nobilo, the source of this document, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is relevant and in the interest of the Defence of your client. The source first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As far as the source of the film is concerned, we would like to stick to the positions we had before. We will indicate the source in the course of the proceeding that will be conducted by the Defence. As for the relevance, this is a mortar shell which is assumed to have come from Stari Vitez and killed eight children on a basketball ground at a time when there was no fighting. As after that date, let us not go into the details. An offensive and attack took place against Stari Vitez of its own initiative, but we will be able to link the two together later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, are you satisfied with this answer? I did not understand very well the first answer regarding the source, the origin of this tape, this video. I understand that you do not wish to indicate a source, but I did not understand when you intend to tell us. Maybe it is a question of translation. Could you repeat your answer regarding the source?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The source is the local television, but we will indicate in specific terms all that is necessary to prove the authenticity of this videotape in the part of the -- in the Defence case, so we ask that the Trial Chamber admit this evidence under the same conditions as it has already admitted other exhibits which the Defence has tendered in the course of the cross-examination; that is on condition that the Defence asserts the grounds later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The judges agree with this manner of proceeding. Mr. Prosecutor, are you agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, Mr. President and your Honours, we still have the issue of relevance. Is it the position of the Defence that Mr. Blaskic is entitled to commit war crimes in retaliation or in response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you cannot intervene with the strategy of the Defence. I think that you put a pertinent question; the Defence has answered it. I have also asked regarding the relevance of the shooting of animals, but the Defence said it was relevant; therefore we can understand the link that was referred to, therefore the objection is rejected. In that case, we will see the video. Turn down the lights and we will ask the Technical Department to show us the video. Mr. Registrar, does the Technical Department have the tape? I apologise for interfering. We have still not decided whether we will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The instructions given at the beginning of the trial, the parties have been asked to submit tapes directly to the technicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Let us continue with the viewing of this tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: "On 10th June 1993 about 8.40 pm on Podgradina opstina Vitez mortar shells, calibre 120 millimetres, shot from positions held by the army of the BH. The following children were killed: Boris Mariko Anticevic, son of Marka, killed on 10th June 1993; Drazen Cecura, the son of Stipe, born on 8th July 1978 in Travnik, a Croat, killed on 10th June 1993; Dragan Ramljak, the son of Vlade, born on 26th June 1978 in Travnik, a Croat, killed on 10th June 1993; Milan Garic, the son of Milka, born on 25th October 1981 in Vitez, a Croat, killed on 10th June 1993; Velimir Grebenar, son of Pere, born on 4th March 1981 in Travnik, a Croat, killed on 10th June 1993; Avgustina Grebenar, daughter of Pere, born on 1st December 1984 in Travnik, a Croat, died in hospital in Nova Bila as a result of the wounds sustained on 10th June 1993; Sanja Krizanovic, daughter of Mirka, born on 14th July 1978 in Travnik, a Croat, died in the hospital in Nova Bila as a result of the wounds sustained on 10th June 1993; Sanja Garic, daughter of Milka, born on 10th October 1975 in Travnik, Croat, died in the hospital in Split on 24th June 1993 as a result of the wounds sustained. In addition to the mentioned children that were killed by the shelling of Vitez on 10th June 1993, the following children were injured: Ivan Garic, born in 1978, Blazenka Cecura, born in 1981; Marina Garic born in 1983; Damir Garic born in 1983. The children who died in the hospitals in Nova Bila and in Split were buried subsequently."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, that would be all. Mr. Djidic, did you order this shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I object? I did not see the entire video film. I saw most of it though, and if I followed what I heard correctly -- I did not see all of it -- it was said that it was 120-millimetre calibre of the mortar shell, and Podgradina is so close to Stari Vitez that such a calibre cannot be used at such short range. I did not even have that calibre of shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That would be all, your Honour. Mr. President, we have just concluded our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor? You have some clarifications to ask of your witness, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just very quickly, Mr. President. I will get through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are they questions which can be put before the break, if I understand well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It might run just a little over the break, your Honour. If your Honour wants to take a break now I can get through it quickly. It will also give me an opportunity to put some of the Defence exhibits just introduced onto the easels, so it might facilitate things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, in that case we will resume work at 11.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Will you please have the accused brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. With the assistance of Mr. Dubuisson, I would like to turn our attention to some of the Defence exhibits that have been discussed during the cross-examination of Mr. Djidic, starting first with D19. Again, there has been no translation of this, so it is just an HVO document coming from the Defence. I think it is easier if it is taken out of the plastic. Mr. Djidic, take a look at this document; this is a document that was discussed during cross-examination concerning an alleged murder that took place on 17th January 1993 with the investigation taking place on 18th January 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just take another look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, it is not easily visible, at least on my monitor. Perhaps you see better? Should I press a button somewhere to make it clearer? Go on, Mr. Prosecutor. We will make do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Djidic, again just to correct myself, this reflects an incident that took place on 17th January 1993 and that was investigated by at least an HVO military judge and Prosecutor on 18th January 1993. Does that document not reflect those facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So this document indicates that as at January of 1993, the HVO had in place a military structure to investigate alleged crimes and to investigate those crimes quickly, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Moving away from this document, your Honour, there were some questions concerning an article that was reflected in D25. Again your Honours there is no translation, it is in Bosnian Serbo-Croatian, and it is an interview of General Alagic. Do you recall this article, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alagic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the article -- if you could, Claudius -- there is no need to put it on the ELMO; just give it to Mr. Djidic -- there is discussion in the article about resupplying Stari Vitez, and Defence counsel asked you whether or not the UN had given any ammunition at all to Stari Vitez during the siege. Did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did you get ammunition from, or resupply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This statement made by Mr. Alagic that, through friends in the UN, he had provided some ammunition, is not correct. No one supplied Stari Vitez with any ammunition on the part of the UN members. I did, on one occasion, receive a small quantity of ammunition, but along the Lasva river, it was sent to me. Who sent that ammunition, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, did you ever get any ammunition in any quantities from any humanitarian aid organisations outside the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, in the discussions, was there any private organisation that provided you with any ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that it was not provided by any United Nations organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What I am asking you is: did you on one occasion get some from a private organisation? Without identifying the private organisation, did you get any from a private organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did get this ammunition that I referred to, that came down the Lasva river, from a private organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But it was not the UN. Was it the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not the UN or the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By Red Cross I am referring to the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right. I understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let us turn our attention to some Defence exhibits, starting with the exhibit to the left, D27. If I can approach this exhibit, Mr. President? Staying with Defence exhibit 27, and in this map Mr. Nobilo drew lines concerning where the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was and the lines with the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This line (indicates) was after 16th April and it changed. I can draw in exactly where the HVO forces were and the army forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a Defence exhibit, so why do you not point to that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I have drawn is that, roughly, that is it, more or less (indicates), but please, if I can ask you for your attention, the HVO was in the village of Zabilje. The HVO was in the village of Krcevine. The HVO was in the village of Jardo. The HVO was in the villages of Ahmici and Pirici. The HVO was in the district of Safredini, and the HVO was in the urban part of the town, throughout the city centre. Similarly, the HVO had a barracks in the mountain lodge called Zabrdje. It is not on the map, it is above Krusica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us point to the area where there is a hook in the map and that is the area Grbavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Grbavica settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the latter part -- you say August/September 1993, did the HVO take this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. At the end of August or the beginning of September, I am not quite sure, the HVO captured the whole of Grbavica and burnt it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Did these lines exist at all prior to the HVO attack on the morning of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not. A part of the HVO lines were regulated in the village of Krcevine. That line remained until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These particular lines though, this particular fighting took place between the HVO and the Armija prior to 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there fighting taking place between the two armies prior to 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the broader area, in this broader area (indicates), no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Several maps have been discussed by Defence counsel and I believe the first one is D21, where, I believe this is November 1992, there were some villages circled where Territorial Defence units were located; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are there soldiers that are working 24 hours a day in these particular villages, waiting for an attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were soldiers who were working in factories, and when they completed their work, they would keep duty in their villages, guard duty in their villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How many Territorial Defence soldiers did you have in the entire Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Vague as to time, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Any time. During this timeframe. How many Territorial Defence soldiers were there during November 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, there is an objection from the Defence. Can you formulate that objection please, Mr. Hayman? I did not understand very well what you said. I understand it is an objection that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The question is vague as to time. We do not know what the time reference is to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, can you answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will stay with the Defence exhibit. During November 1992 as exhibited in Defence exhibit 21, how many Territorial Defence soldiers did you have in the entire municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact number. We were in the process of forming a brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After the brigade was formed, can you give us an approximate number how many there were in the entire municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty troops that went to the front consisted of about 1,000 to 1,500 men. I am not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This included men that went to the front and were fighting against the Serbs on the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This other map, I guess, is in 1992/1993, October 1992 to 1993, that reflects the 325th -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was December 1992 and January 1993; that is what it says on the map anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I stand corrected; it does say December 1992/January 1993. This reflects various villages that supplied the brigades, or the 325th Brigade, with headquarters, at Poculice and Krusica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these are the localities which supplied the members of the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Taking these two maps together, Defence counsel indicated that he was attempting to demonstrate that the HVO was surrounded during this period of time, and were these soldiers sitting there just surrounding Vitez, waiting to attack the HVO in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, certainly not. When you see the distribution of the HVO troops and their barracks, then the picture becomes quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So the record is clear, your Honour, I believe the last exhibit referred to by counsel and the witness but not in the record is map D23.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour, this map is D23; the map of the Territorial Defence is D21. Your Honours, this is the top portion of exhibit 29 as received in evidence, the map that is leaning on the wall behind your Honours. This is just a xeroxed top of that. Mr. Djidic, using this red pen, show us where the HVO was located in and around Vitez. Mark all the villages, all the locations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the town of Vitez itself; the school in Dubravica; the bungalow in Nadioci; the hunting lodge near Novaci and near the petrol station Kaleb; then in Krusica, the Ribnjak Hotel and the Lovac Hotel; the mountain lodge at Zabrdje; Bistrovo between Krusica and Zabrdje where they had exercise grounds for the training in private weekend homes, from which the owners were thrown out by the HVO. In the town of Vitez itself, in the building of the police station, the regional HVO police was headquartered. And in the old school, that was where the HVO military police was based, about 50 metres from there, in the building of the cinema, the HVO brigade command. In the building of the hotel, the command of the region of Central Bosnia of the HVO. Then Mali Mosulj, Veceriska, and next to Veceriska is the factory where the special taskforce was based for protecting the factory. A large unit was based in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to the factory. The factory, where is that located? Where is that unit in the factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is between the village of Veceriska and the village of Gacice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In cross-examination, Defence counsel asked you about an alleged incident where some Muslim apparently attempted to damage an HVO facility in Gacice; do you recall that? Was there an HVO facility in Gacice, or was it Donje Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Donje Veceriska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were talking about Nova Bila. Were there any other facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nova Bila is not in the territory of the Vitez municipality, but it is a factory of the timber industry, where the HVO army was accommodated. I do not know exactly how many men were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Any other locations where the HVO had a military installation other than these? Just in this general area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were other locations, but it is interesting to note that all the units formed in the Vitez municipality came from specific villages which had a mixed population, such as, for instance, Dubravica, Ahmici, and Nadioci; Veceriska, Krusica, Rijeka --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us distinguish these. You had the pink or the red down as military facilities. Now you are mentioning villages similar to Defence exhibits 21 and 23 that supplied the HVO. You mentioned some of those villages and one I think will be Dubravica, another one was Ahmici; what other villages supplied the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These barracks that I have indicated, the ones in Zabrdje, Dubravica, the town of Vitez itself, and, of course, they also came from nearby places around these.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Krusica? Whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am talking about the towns of Busovaca, Travnik, Novi Travnik and so on and, of course, Krusica as well, which had three facilities for the accommodation of troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that all of these villages in this map supplied troops to the HVO in the Lasva valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that -- to encompass this entire area and say they all supply troops to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the whole area, the entire municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This map does not include the entire municipality of Vitez, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map does cover the entire territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This entire map supplies the HVO. However, Senez is not in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In discussing that map and in discussing Defence exhibits 21 and 23, was it in the interests of the Bosnian Muslims to be preparing to attack and to attack the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was never in their interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, at the beginning of my testimony, I said that we in Vitez, before the elections, lived very well with our neighbours. Secondly, an aggression was carried out against Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Serbs, and we joined in the Defence. Thirdly, we had orders, under no circumstances were we to clash with the HVO, and we followed those orders to the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know why that order was given not to clash with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was because of all these other things that I mentioned in the interest of good neighbourly relations, and attempts for us to jointly fight against the same enemy until the liberation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who was that joint enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just move to a xeroxed copy of what has already been introduced in evidence as Prosecutor's exhibit 45. Prior to doing that, Mr. Dubuisson, with your permission -- your Honour, what is the Prosecutor's next number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Gregory, I would like to ask your Honours for me to correct the last words I uttered. When I said that it was the Serbs that had attacked, I should like to correct myself, and say the attacks were carried out by the Chetniks, because all Serbs are not Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djidic. Your Honour, the exhibit, I believe, is Prosecutor's exhibit 83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like us to hear your whole response, Mr. Kehoe. We are not going to repeat the whole examination. It is a replica, based on the cross-examination of the Defence, so let us be careful. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours, and I will be brief. I was just attempting to clarify some issues that came through in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Then continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may approach the easel, your Honour, with a xerox copy of Prosecutor's exhibit 45, which will be 45A. Using Prosecutor's exhibit 45A, you were asked on cross-examination about the location of your headquarters, the two locations of your headquarters and also the location of your ammunition depot. I believe you noted that on the exhibit that is a larger exhibit than this. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Using a red pen, could you locate on this exhibit the two locations of your headquarters, marking the first one as 1 and the second one as 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is it (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Using the green, could you please mark the location of your ammunition depot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is it (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Lastly, with the red marker, could you please outline what you can see on here are your trenches, the defensive positions, that you built up over time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the war, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. The rest of Stari Vitez is cut off from this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. A bit is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Looking at this particular exhibit, you were asked some questions on cross-examination concerning the shooting of Marko Prskalo and another person that were at negotiations at BritBat that took place in front of the hotel Vitez marked by exhibit A; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is an entrance to the hotel Vitez here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Vitez hotel had a few entrances. The main entrance was on this side (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: From your frontline, did you have every entrance in and out of the hotel Vitez covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had them covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you have the back side covered as well as the front or just the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Asked and answered, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not cover a single entrance, only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What exactly did you have? He is explaining his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not cover a single entrance into the hotel, only part of the street in the vicinity of the entrance to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You are marking on the exhibit with a red marker next to the marker A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the entrance. I think there is about 30 metres there. Here to here, from the street to the entrance to the hotel (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on this drawing, could your soldiers here cover the back entrance on the back street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot hear the interpreter well. Better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on the drawing that you just made on this street, could your line cover the entrance on the back street coming into the hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could not cover that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Have a seat. You were asked some questions on cross-examination about the offer of the HVO for civilians to leave Stari Vitez. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were ultimatums to surrender and to evacuate civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had the shelling of Stari Vitez already started before these ultimatums were given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were asked in cross-examination about whether or not it would have been better for civilians to be taken from Novaci and secured in the Dubravica school; do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it have been better for those civilians if their homes had not been burnt in the first place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, it would have been better had they not been attacked at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would that likewise be true of all the villages in the Lasva valley? Would it not have been better for those civilians if their houses had not been attacked and burned in the first place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please do not make any comments; just put questions. If you have something to say to the witness, ask him a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. You were asked some questions about ammunition and houses by the Defence counsel; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were also asked questions about ammunition in your ammunition depot. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You also said that ammunition was taken by soldiers to their individual homes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ammunition is given out together with rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did each soldier have large stores of ammunition in his home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct to say that they had about 100 bullets per person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, Defence counsel asked you some questions concerning orders given by Blaskic concerning sniper attacks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the sniper attacks continue -- the sniper shooting continue through the 11-month siege?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were short periods of time when HVO snipers did not operate really, but most of the time, throughout the war, snipers were in operation; that is to say in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You mentioned some individuals during your direct examination that were shot by sniper attacks. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show you a photograph. (Handed). Do you recognise those two people, Mr. Djidic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are a husband and wife. I think they were killed in June 1993, by sniper shooting. They were around 70 years old, they were in their garden, and they were killed within one hour only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they soldiers fighting in trenches, Mr. Djidic, or were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were civilians. I already said they were over 70, I believe. When they were killed they were in their garden. They were doing something, I do not know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have one moment? (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor? The judges would like to see the following -- that is we would like to ask you to remain within the bounds of the cross-examination, please. Your reply, or at least that is the wish of the judges, that your reply sticks strictly to new elements that arose during the cross-examination, which means two things: first, you must not make the witness restate all that he has already said, because we have already been listening to this witness for several days, and only new elements are of interest to the judges, not elements which were already indicated. That is the observation of the judges. Continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have completed my redirect examination and just ask the court to move into evidence exhibits 84, 85 and the map, which is 45A, the top sheet which is a xerox copy of an exhibit that is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which are they? I was told that it was 85; is that correct? So the small photographs will be admitted as Prosecution exhibits number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The small photographs are document 85; the map which is up there on the board is 85A, and the one below is 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which is the origin of exhibit 85, Mr. Prosecutor, that is the photograph of civilians, the husband and wife killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The origin of that photograph, your Honour, are photographs given to us by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I believe there is one correction concerning what Mr. Dubuisson said, I believe the map facing us on the easel is 45A and I believe you said 85A. I am not sure if it was in the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, it is 45A, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have you finished, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am sorry to take the floor once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In principle, I do not think you can have the floor again, but I will consult my colleagues. (Pause). Mr. Nobilo, the Trial Chamber will abide by the principle it has established. This is a witness of the Prosecution; the Prosecution examined him, you cross-examined and the Prosecution had a redirect, therefore you do not have the right to speak again. I will ask my colleagues whether they have any questions to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we respect that. We would simply like to note that the witness has changed his testimony with respect to sources of ammunition and so in effect we were not able to effectively cross-examine him about his earlier testimony, because he now changed his testimony on redirect examination. I simply wish to state --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, the Trial Chamber has taken a decision. The Trial Chamber knows how to read the transcript. We have had four and a half days of testimony and now it is up to the Trial Chamber to decide that the witness has been examined in direct, cross-examined and there was a redirect. I think there has to be a certain order and certain rules. If the witness has changed his testimony, the judges will see that and I assume you can refer to that in your closing statement. It is now the turn of my colleagues if they wish to put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, in the course of your testimony, I think it was on Tuesday 28th, you referred to an official ceremony when General Blaskic was present, and at which a speech was made by Dario Kordic, a speech that you did not like at all because -- I am almost citing what you said -- "he rejected coexistence between the communities in Bosnia and claimed the right to Bosnia solely for the Croatian nation." That is in the transcript, the English transcript. Can you tell us what was the exact role of General Blaskic at that official ceremony that you described to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic was present and he did not speak. Kordic spoke, Santic spoke, Cerkez spoke, and in his speech, Kordic said, as far as Herceg-Bosna is concerned, that which you asked me about in connection with Bosnia, so he said that in connection with Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The others who spoke at that ceremony, did they repeat the same propositions as Kordic supported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Then, later on, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can we have the translation of what the witness said? I think he said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: During that ceremony, were the same propositions made by other people, by politicians, or military men; were the same statements and claims on Herceg-Bosna exclusively for the Croats and the ending of Muslim presence there -- were the same propositions set forth by others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but they did not repeat what Kordic had said. He was the most extremist of all, and all the statements were similar in connection with Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In other words, it was a policy that was pursued and not an isolated case that was evidenced during that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The speeches were welcomed by a lot of applause.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the media support these same claims following this ceremony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before the ceremony and after the ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there any precise measures taken to realise these claims or what has been known as ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What were these measures and procedures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were political procedures by the HDZ concerning that which I spoke of. The establishment of HVO government which belonged to a single nation, a single ethnic group, the elimination of Muslims from government, and the implementation of all those things which related to the political and military establishment of a state within a state, that is to say Herceg-Bosna within Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In your testimony also on the 28th in the afternoon in the French transcript, page 721, you added that places of worship, Muslim places of worship, were particularly and deliberately destroyed, and not only the houses and the property of the Muslims, and you stated that this was a pre-established and concerted plan that was being implemented. Perhaps you could give us the indicators which led you to make such a conclusion that this was an established plan, not only an armed conflict that results in mutual destruction or reciprocal destruction on both sides.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I shall try to explain this to you. The places of worship of the Muslims were desecrated before the war, during the war and after the war, that is to say even after a cease-fire had been signed with the HVO, and the objective was to destroy the history of the Muslims, and proof of the existence of Muslims in this territory. This can be seen even now everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What would you wish to imply when you say "now and everywhere"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, also when you look at Bosnia, specifically Central Bosnia in Vitez, you can see destroyed places of worship because they have not been repaired yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In connection with the incident of the shell that was shown to us on video today, did this incident, as far as you know, take place before the destruction of those places of worship and civilian homes, or did it take place after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The destruction in Central Bosnia lasted 11 months. The attacks on Stari Vitez were underway for 11 months, not every day though; that is to say that there was destruction before and after the incident that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEN
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, you described the siege of Stari Vitez and you told us that it endured for 11 months. You also indicated that during that period, there were some Croats in Stari Vitez. Did they remain until the end of the siege?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did, part of them. Part of the Croats had left Stari Vitez before the attack on Stari Vitez. Part of the Croats left when the exchange took place of the civilians detained in the cinema. A smaller part left then. During the conflict itself in Stari Vitez, about 45 Croats remained and three Serbs too. Most of them still live in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the Croats and the three Serbs who remained in Stari Vitez participate in the resistance offered by Stari Vitez to the attacks against Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you say whether any of the houses belonging to Croats and Serbs in Stari Vitez were damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: About what proportion of those houses would you say were damaged, half or a quarter, or a third?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps a quarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I ask you to turn to another phase of the evidence, during which you referred to what you described as the expulsion of Muslims from the Vitez area proper, and an issue was raised as to whether they had been expelled or whether they left voluntarily. Do you remember that phase of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I do remember that, and it is true that people were expelled. A small number of people left voluntarily; however the majority were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you say whether any of those Muslims who you say were expelled returned to Vitez after the siege was lifted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no one has ever returned to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last question relating to the video clip which Mr. Nobilo showed us towards the end of his cross-examination. When he was asked by the President, he indicated that those clips had been taken by a local television station, I think. Did any TV station enter Stari Vitez during the 11-month period of the siege?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you have any clips or are you aware of the existence of any clips, video clips, taken by those TV stations of occurrences within Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have some video clips from a joint meeting when Mr. Petkovic came to Stari Vitez, as well as Mr. Halilovic, with their teams, and I have a video clip from the funeral of 105 people who were buried in Stari Vitez. I gave the Prosecutor this videocassette. I do not know if it was admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Riad, you have another question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, during your stay in Vitez, you were able to note to what extent it was possible to know what was happening in the surrounding villages, to what extent could one hear the explosions and to be au courant as to what was happening throughout the valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could notice when bombings and shellings took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Up to what distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the distance in one part nearest Stari Vitez, one could see the village of Krcevine quite well. Also there is a good view of Grbavica, there is a good view of Donja Veceriska, the village of Gacice, Bradina and Novaci. In other places people could hear shooting and they could hear the direction from which it was coming, and also smoke from grenades and from places that were burning could be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Djidic, the Tribunal wishes to thank you for coming and testifying for four days. We appreciate your testimony and you are now discharged. Will you please accompany Mr. Djidic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is 12.45. Mr. Prosecutor, would you prefer that we have the next witness brought in now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would prefer -- I think it would be easier your Honour if we take a break now and then just start up earlier and we can get right through it quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is fine. Very well, in that case the hearing is adjourned and we will resume at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please bring in the accused. The hearing is resumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, your Honours, before I begin on the next witness, talking to Mr. Djidic at the lunch break, he would like to clarify one point, and the point is that, with regard to the ammunition, he did get ammunition down the river, but he said that on one occasion, he did get ammunition from a private entity, not the United Nations, not the Red Cross, in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, that is all very fine. I think, nevertheless, that Mr. Djidic had things to say, he had ample time to do so. Either we bring Mr. Djidic back into the courtroom, if he is still here, but for that I will consult my colleagues, but you cannot bring us suggestions from Mr. Djidic again which we are going to discuss, ask the Defence for their opinion and so on. Mr. Kehoe, we are professionals, agreed? That is the first point. Is Mr. Djidic still here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I am going to consult my colleagues then. (Pause).
